_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/transactions?format=json
(two waiver-claim transactions extracted from that collection)
REDACTION: all identifiers invented. Player names are real NFL players with
PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED numeric ids.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — THE FAAB PAIR. Transaction 156 carries
faab_bid "17". Transaction 157 carries faab_bid "0" — a real, winning zero
bid, which is how an uncontested claim is settled in a FAAB league. Neither
may be confused with the ABSENT faab_bid in yahoo_transaction_add_drop.json,
which means Yahoo did not state a bid at all. Three states, one column:
faab_bid "17"  → 17
faab_bid "0"   → 0     (a genuine zero — NOT 'no bid')
<no faab_bid>  → NULL  (not exposed — NOT a zero bid)
Collapse the last two and every FAAB-spend analysis is silently wrong: teams
that never bid look identical to teams that won everything for free, and the
rows still validate. ⚠️ NOTE FOR THE READER: Yahoo documents faab_bid only as
a WRITE input on the transaction POST. Whether it is returned on a GET of a
processed claim is UNVERIFIED — no live call has been made. If a real capture
shows it absent, that is a genuine provider limitation to record in the
completeness report, and this fixture must be corrected rather than trusted.
SECOND CLAIM THIS FILE MAKES: a waiver add has source_type 'waivers' and NO
source_team_key. The player came from the waiver pool, not from a team, so
the concept does not apply and the key is absent rather than empty. That
absence is the only thing separating a waiver claim from a free-agent pickup
once the rows are in the database — 'freeagents' vs 'waivers' plus the
missing key IS the distinction. Do not fill it with ''.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. transactions is a numeric-key COLLECTION with a sibling 'count'.
2. transaction_data is a BARE DICT (add/drop family, not the trade family).
3. Player metadata is a LIST NESTED INSIDE the player resource array, one
single-key dict per field.
4. Transaction 157 also carries waiver_priority "4" as a bare INT while
faab_bid is a STRING in the same object — Yahoo's types are inconsistent
within a single node, which is why every field is coerced explicitly.
5. Losing waiver claims DO NOT APPEAR HERE AND CANNOT. Yahoo exposes only
successful transactions; the competing bids are gone the moment waivers
process. That is a permanent provider gap, recorded as not_exposed in
the completeness report — never as 'no one else bid'.
NOT TRUNCATED: two complete transactions, isolated from the surrounding
collection so a failure is unambiguous.
